eli5.text: Starting today, the system now routes to a specific Fireworks model (accounts/james-65d217/deployments/lnfid5h9) instead of the previously tested minimax-m2p5 model, and the time-based restriction that previously limited deployment to 10 AM to 8 PM Eastern Time has been removed entirely. This change affects the agent's model selection behavior, as well as the base agent prompt which now mandates suggesting follow-ups for all user questions, even when the conversation is fast-paced. If you looked, you would notice that the model identifier in the test script has been switched from minimax-m2p5 to the new deployment ID, the time gate function always returns true, and the agent instruction now requires follow-up suggestions without exceptions for speed mode.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.22 released
ai.summary: Version 0.0.22 of the freebuff CLI package was published, bumping the version string in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.0.21 to 0.0.22 as part of a release-bump commit. This release bundles several user-visible improvements from the same-day commit sequence: the Fireworks custom deployment accounts/james-65d217/deployments/lnfid5h9 was activated in scripts/test-fireworks-long.ts with isDeploymentHours() returning true, the base agent prompt in agents/base2/base2.ts made suggest_followups mandatory for questions, the ChatGPT connect banner in cli/src/components/chatgpt-connect-banner.tsx gained an interactive x close button calling setInputMode('default'), the CLI help banner in cli/src/components/help-banner.tsx now displays a /interview to /plan to implement to /review workflow tip when ChatGPT OAuth is connected, and the set_output handler now parses raw fields first then falls back to output.data while selecting the Zod parse attempt with fewer issues. The package.json change is the canonical version marker for this release, incrementing the top-level version field from 0.0.21 to 0.0.22 in the release packaging manifest only.
ai.evidence: Commit [03655ce1] bumps the version field from 0.0.21 to 0.0.22 in freebuff/cli/release/package.json. This is the release-bump commit for version 0.0.22, which aggregates the previous same-day work including Fireworks deployment activation, mandatory ChatGPT followups, ChatGPT connect banner close button, CLI help workflow tips, and set_output schema parsing improvements. The commit modifies only the version string in the release package manifest.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.22 adds a smoother, friendlier setup for connecting your ChatGPT account and picks a smarter AI model to run behind-the-scenes tests, so you get more accurate help with less friction. When you open the app, the welcome screen now shows clear next steps if your ChatGPT is already linked (for example a tip that says start with /interview then move to /plan), and the old message asking you to connect just got a real X button so you can close it quickly instead of hunting for the escape key. Under the hood, Freebuff now supports sending output in two different formats, so tools that follow strict data rules still work, and follow-up questions are always suggested for tricky prompts, meaning you are less likely to get stuck mid-conversation. Upgrading gives you a cleaner first-time experience, fewer error messages, and a slightly smarter helper that knows when it should offer next steps, all without changing the way you already use Freebuff.

ai.title: Remove isDeploymentHours from Fireworks deployment routing tests
ai.summary: Removed `isDeploymentHours` import and its 8 test cases from `web/src/llm-api/__tests__/fireworks-deployment.test.ts`. Replaced the `uses standard API outside deployment hours` test with `uses standard API when custom deployment is disabled`, switching from a time-based spy to an explicit `useCustomDeployment: false` flag. Scope: Fireworks deployment routing tests only. Detail: the routing decision moved from implicit ET-hour gating to an explicit boolean parameter.

eli5.text: The system that tests how requests are routed for a specific AI provider has been simplified. Previously, tests checked whether requests were routed based on the time of day (in Eastern Time), but now they test that routing is decided by an explicit on/off switch instead. This means the tests no longer rely on simulating different times of day to verify behavior; they just check whether custom routing is enabled or disabled through a clear flag. This is behind-the-scenes cleanup that makes the tests easier to understand and maintain.

ai.title: Reinstate custom deployment hours
ai.summary: The `isDeploymentHours` function in `web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts` now enforces the 10:00-20:00 ET window by returning the calculated boolean instead of hardcoded `true`. This change restores the intended time-gating logic for custom deployments, which was previously bypassed by the temporary override. The modification affects only the Web surface via the LLM API integration.

eli5.text: Starting today, the web assistant once again respects the 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM Eastern Time window when deciding whether to use its advanced AI model. If you open the web app before 10 AM or after 8 PM Eastern, you will automatically get the standard model instead of the premium one. This is the same time-based rule that was temporarily turned off, and it only affects people using the assistant through the website.
